accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the principal features associated with Lord Cornwallis's civil service reforms in India?
o: A military service based on hereditary succession and private trade
A merit-based covenanted service, prohibition of private trade and gifts, and promotion by seniority
A wholly Indian civil service recruited through provincial elections
A service recruited exclusively through examinations conducted in India
accepted.x: Cornwallis established a merit-based covenanted civil service, prohibited private trade and acceptance of gifts, and introduced promotion substantially based on seniority.
accepted.tq: Use the cluster of reforms associated with the correct administrator rather than relying on a single keyword.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The College of Fort William was established at Calcutta in 1800 primarily for which of the following purposes?
o: Administering the Provincial Public Service Commission
Conducting the first simultaneous ICS examination
Training only Indian judges in customary law
Training recruits of the Company's civil service
accepted.x: Wellesley established the College of Fort William at Calcutta in 1800 to train recruits of the Company's civil service.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its specific administrative function and founder.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Charter Act of 1853 is significant in the history of the Indian civil services because it:
o: Established the Indian Civil Service exclusively for Indians
Transferred the ICS examination from London to Allahabad
Created the Federal Public Service Commission
Abolished the patronage system and introduced open competitive examination
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1853 abolished appointments by patronage of the Company's Directors and introduced open competitive examination for the civil services.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative change directly linked with the named Act, while rejecting later institutional developments.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Macaulay Committee report:
1. It recommended that the civil service examination should be conducted in London.
2. It favoured preference for graduates of Oxford and Cambridge.
3. It recommended continuation of appointments solely through the patronage of Company Directors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Macaulay recommendations were associated with competitive examination, not continuation of the Company's patronage system.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reform by confusing competitive recruitment with patronage.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indian Civil Services Act of 1861 provided for which of the following?
o: Replacement of the ICS by the IAS
Abolition of all civil service examinations in London
Immediate parity between Indians and Europeans in all covenanted posts
Limited Indian entry, mainly into uncovenanted posts, subject to conditions including residence and language examination
accepted.x: The Indian Civil Services Act of 1861 allowed limited Indian entry, mainly into uncovenanted posts, with conditions including seven years' residence and an examination in the local language.
accepted.tq: Separate limited statutory entry from the later policy of Indianisation and post-1947 changes.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the reduction in the maximum age limit for the civil service examination?
o: 23 years in 1859, 22 years in 1860, 21 years in 1866 and 19 years in 1878
23 years in 1859, 21 years in 1860, 22 years in 1866 and 19 years in 1878
22 years in 1859, 23 years in 1860, 21 years in 1866 and 19 years in 1878
23 years in 1859, 22 years in 1860, 19 years in 1866 and 21 years in 1878
accepted.x: The maximum age was reduced successively from 23 in 1859 to 22 in 1860, 21 in 1866 and 19 in 1878. The reduction under Lytton became a major Indian grievance.
accepted.tq: Track both the numerical trend and the corresponding years before comparing the sequences.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The reduction of the maximum age for the civil service examination to 19 years in 1878 was associated with the tenure of:
accepted.x: The maximum age was reduced to 19 in 1878 during the tenure of Lord Lytton, and this became an important Indian grievance.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical change to the Viceroy in office when it occurred.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The demand for raising the age limit and holding the civil service examination simultaneously in India and England was taken up by the Indian National Congress from:
accepted.x: The INC began pressing these demands from its first session in 1885.
accepted.tq: Use the earliest stated organisational milestone rather than the later date of implementation.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Aitchison Public Service Commission was appointed in 1886 during the viceroyalty of Dufferin. Islington belonged to 1912–15 under Hardinge II, while Lee belonged to 1923–24 under Reading.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure year–commission pair and eliminate options that swap the commissions and Viceroys.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The Aitchison Public Service Commission is associated with which of the following recommendations or changes?
1. Dropping the terms 'covenanted' and 'uncovenanted' services.
2. Classification into Imperial, Provincial and Subordinate services.
3. Raising the age limit to 23 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Aitchison Commission dropped the covenanted–uncovenanted terminology, proposed the three-level classification of services and raised the age limit to 23 years.
accepted.tq: Verify each commission feature independently instead of associating all civil service reforms with one Act.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal objective associated with the Islington Commission of 1912–15 was:
o: Abolition of the Provincial and Subordinate services
Indianisation of higher civil service posts
Introduction of patronage appointments by Company Directors
Creation of the IAS after independence
accepted.x: The Islington Commission, appointed during the tenure of Hardinge II, dealt principally with the Indianisation of higher posts.
accepted.tq: Identify the commission by its central recommendation, not merely by its date.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lee Commission:
1. It was appointed in 1923–24 during the viceroyalty of Lord Reading.
2. It proposed 50:50 Indian-European parity in the ICS within 15 years.
3. Its recommendations were unrelated to the creation of a Public Service Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Lee Commission was also associated with the establishment of a Public Service Commission, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the negative statement that disconnects a commission from an institutional consequence expressly associated with it.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On which date was the Public Service Commission established in connection with the recommendations of the Lee Commission?
accepted.x: The Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926 in the context of the Lee Commission's recommendations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise institutional date from the dates of the Lee Commission and later constitutional changes.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relevant civil service provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: It established the Federal Public Service Commission in place of all provincial services.
It abolished the ICS and created the IAS with immediate effect.
It provided for a separate ICS examination in India, enabling simultaneous examinations with England from 1922.
It restored the exclusive patronage of the Company's Directors over civil service appointments.
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1919, provided for a separate ICS examination in India; simultaneous examinations were held from 1922, alongside the London examination.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the enabling legal provision from the later date of actual examination and from post-independence reforms.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the examination arrangements for the Indian Civil Service, consider the following statements:
1. Examinations were held in India at Allahabad from 1922.
2. Delhi later became the Indian venue.
3. The London examination was discontinued when the Indian examination began.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Indian examination began at Allahabad in 1922 and was later held at Delhi, alongside the examination in London. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Watch for the false discontinuity claim in a question about simultaneous arrangements.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1950 — UPSC replaced the Federal Public Service Commission
Government of India Act, 1919 — UPSC replaced the Federal Public Service Commission
Government of India Act, 1935 — Federal Public Service Commission and Provincial Public Service Commissions
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1919, dealt with the provision for a separate ICS examination in India. The Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions were provided for by the 1935 Act, and UPSC replaced the Federal PSC in 1950.
accepted.tq: Find the option that assigns a later constitutional development to the wrong Act.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who described the Indian Civil Service as the 'Steel Frame' of India?
accepted.x: Sardar Patel described the Indian Civil Service as the 'Steel Frame' of India.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the statesman associated with it.
accepted.sec: Civil services - Cornwallis, Haileybury, ICS age, simultaneous exams, commissions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly explains the statutory civil service scheme introduced under Lord Lytton in 1878–79?
o: One-half of the ICS posts were reserved for Indians under the Lee Commission.
All covenanted posts were opened equally to Indians and Europeans through local examinations.
One-sixth of the covenanted posts were set aside for Indians of high families, and the scheme was later abolished.
The scheme transferred all civil service appointments to elected provincial governments.
accepted.x: Lytton's statutory civil service scheme reserved one-sixth of covenanted posts for Indians of high families; it was later abolished. It did not establish complete equality or the later 50:50 parity proposal.
accepted.tq: Separate the limited statutory concession under Lytton from the later Lee Commission parity proposal.
